instructions.data_entry:
*Please select a folder to store your inputs in.
*Folder should be named with the test name and contain LEMS raw data (labeled foldername_RawData and saved as a csv file) if using.
*To enter values for charcoal created by wood stoves, please enter the information as a second or third fuel in Fuel
*with a cfrac db of greater than 0.75. Then enter charcoal weights as a fuel mass with the initial mass being 0 if the stove started with no charcoal.
*Default values for charcoal created in a wood stove are:
   mc (moisure content): 0%
   higher heating value: 32500kJ/kg
   cfrac db (carbon fraction on a dry basis): 0.9
*The carbon fraction for wood is typically 0.5g/kg
*The correction value calculates the lower heating value of the fuel. For wood it is 1320, for charcoal is it 1200, for kerosene it is 2600, for LPG it is 3300.
*For max water temperature, enter the maximum temperature of the water.
*For end water temperature enter the temperature of the water at the end of the phase (at the end of shutdown for ISO tests).
*Please enter all times as either yyyymmdd HH:MM:SS or HH:MM:SS and enter all times in the same format.
*Names highlighted in green are required entries. Names highlighted in yellow are highly recommended entries.
*Entry spaces highlighted in red or yellow have invalid or blank inputs for required or recommended fields. Entry spaces highlighted in green have valid inputs for required or recommended fields.
instructions.browse_info:
To select a folder to store data, click the browse button above.

Test information is not required and will not impact calculations but it is recommended in order to easily track tests.
instructions.enviro:
Environmental information is required to properly calcualte thermal efficinecy.
Please refer to ISO protocol for required environmental information.

Pot dry mass refers to the mass of the pot with no water in it.
instructions.fuel:
Fuel information requires the species name (fuel type), the moisture content of the fuel (fuel mc), the high heating value, and the carbon fraction on a dry basis (fuel cfrac db).

For wood, the carbon fraction is typically 0.5.

For charcoal, the carbon fraction is typlically 0.9.

For wood stoves, charcoal created by the stove is entered as fuel 2 with a moisture content of 0.

For fuels other than wood or charcoal, please refer to the standard for heating values and carbon fraction.

The correction value is the energy required to vaporize water created by the combustion of hydrogen in the fuel. For wood this is typically 1320 kJ/kg and for charcoal this is typically 1200 kJ/kg.
instructions.high_power:
Variables highlighted in green are required entries. Variables highlighted in yellow are recommended entries.

High power end time is the end of the shutdown phase for ISO tests.

End of phase temperature is the temperature at the end of the shutdown phase for ISO tests.
instructions.weighting:
Weighting tiers are used to create weighted averages of performance metrics.
If you have field data that shows usage rates of each power level (high, medium, low), you may enter values that reflect that.
If you do not have field data, enter 1 for each phase performed during the test.
If you are using a single power stove, enter 1 for weight hp and 0 for all other phases.
Sum numbers for weight total.
instructions.gas_check:
GAS CHECK INSTRUCTIONS:
The following entries are for checking gas sensor bias and drift over a test period.
Only enter values for spans that were performed during testing.
Pre-test and post-test values are required to calculate sensor drift.
If you do not want to check drift, leave pre and post values blank.
Pre-test spans should be close to span gas concentrations.
Drift check calculates percent change between pre and post-test values. Value should be less than 5%.
Select which sensors to calibrate in the bottom right corner. Calibration is only required if sensor bias is large.
instructions.leak_check:
LEAK CHECK INSTRUCTIONS:
The following entries are for checking system leaks.
Please enter pressure drop values and times for each test performed.
Gravimetric leak checks are calculated as a leak rate.
Pressure sensor leak checks are calculated as a percent pressure change.
All leak checks must pass to meet ISO standards.
instructions.pm_check:
PM2.5 QUALITY CONTROL INSTRUCTIONS:
The following entries are for checking gravimetric and black carbon flow and sampling quality.
Gravimetric flow change must be less than 5% to meet ISO standards.
Balance calibration and filter weights must be recorded according to SOPs.
instructions.add_check:
ADDITIONAL CHECK INSTRUCTIONS:
The following entries are additional ISO quality control checks.
Induced draft is only needed for chimney stoves.
Total capture should be observed during the duration of the test.
instructions.menu:
* Please use the following buttons in order to process your data.
* Buttons will turn green when successful.
* Buttons will turn red when unsuccessful.
* Tabs will appear which will contain outputs from each step.
* If data from a previous step is changed, all proceeding steps must be done again.
* Files with data outputs will appear in the folder you selected. Modifying these files will change the calculated result if steps are redone.

DO NOT proceed with the next step until the previous step is successful.
If a step is unsuccessful and all instructions from the error message have been followed or no error message appears, send a screenshot of the print out in your python interpreter or the second screen (black with white writing if using the app version) along with your data to jaden@aprovecho.org.
instructions.menu_bc: To process black carbon data. Take filter pictures according to instructions. Save pictures in test folder and name files as foldername_filternumber where the filter number correlates with the filter ID used during gravimetric calculations.

Program was unable to read the raw data file correctly. Please check the following:
    * There are no blank lines or cells within the data set
    * The sensor box was not reset at some point causing a header to be inserted into the middle of the data set.
    * There are no extra blank lines or non value lines at the end of the file.
Opening the file in a text editing program like notepad may be helpful. Delete problems and try again.

    * Check that the entered time exists within the data
    * Check that the time has not been left blank when there should be an entry.
The file {path} may need to be opened and changed or deleted.

msg.bkg.edit_methods:
Edit background subtraction methods

Format = method,offset
Methods: pre, post, prepostave, prepostlin, none

Pre: average of pre-background subtracted from data
Post: average of post-background subtracted from data
Prepostave: average of pre and post background subtracted from data
Prepostlin: linear fit between average pre and post background values
None: no background subtraction applied

Preferred method (if pre and post background periods are flat): PREPOSTLIN

Offset: value added to data after background subtraction

Click OK to update plot
Click Cancel to exit
msg.bkg.incorrect_method_entry:
INCORRECT BACKGROUND METHOD ENTRY

Ensure background methods are entered in the correct format with valid numbers and methods

Format = method,offset
Methods: pre, post, prepostave, prepostlin, none

Pre: average of pre-background subtracted from data
Post: average of post-background subtracted from data
Prepostave: average of pre and post background subtracted from data
Prepostlin: linear fit between average pre and post background values
None: no background subtraction applied

Preferred method (if pre and post background periods are flat): PREPOSTLIN

Offset: value added to data after background subtraction

Click OK to update plot
Click Cancel to exit
